title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: A fast Sichuan-style stir-fry of tender chicken, peanuts, dried chiles and scallions in a tangy, slightly sweet soy glaze.

image.alt: A bowl of kung pao chicken with peanuts, dried chiles and green onion

items.item: rice vinegar or Chinese black vinegar

items.prep: snipped in half, seeds shaken out

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and cornstarch and let it sit for {time 10 min}. Stir the sauce ingredients together with {qty 2 tbsp} water in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium heat. Add the chiles and Sichuan pepper and stir until the chiles darken and smell toasty, {time 30 sec}. Don’t let them blacken.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and spread it out. Sear for {time 1 min}, then stir-fry until no longer pink outside, {time 2-3 min}.
Add the garlic, ginger and scallions and stir-fry for {time 1 min}.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and toss until it thickens and coats the chicken and the chicken is cooked through, {time 1-2 min}. Toss in the peanuts and serve with rice.

notes: The dried chiles flavor the oil; most people don’t eat them.
Sichuan peppercorns give a gentle tingling numbness; leave them out for a milder dish.
